D001_l001.question:
A 50-year-old married female, employed as a Human Resources Director, presents with a 1-year and 5-month history of symptoms characterized by significant inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. The patient reports frequent careless mistakes and difficulty sustaining attention during tasks. She acknowledges being forgetful in daily activities, struggles with following through on instructions, and is easily distracted by external stimuli or unrelated thoughts.

Regarding hyperactivity and impulsivity, the patient often fidgets, experiences an inner sense of restlessness, and reports difficulty engaging in quiet leisure activities. She describes often feeling "on the go" as if "driven by a motor." Additionally, she frequently interrupts others and exhibits difficulty waiting her turn in conversations and activities. These symptoms have led to notable functional impairment and were present prior to 12 years of age.
D001_l001.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

S001.examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.examples: Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.

S010.examples: Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S014.name: Constant_Activity

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
